frequency_question: What proportion of recipient nations successfully establish domestic production of complex imported missile systems within two years of acquisition?
membership_rule: Includes any sovereign state that received foreign transfers of advanced cruise missiles or precision strike systems and attempted or achieved domestic industrial replication within 36 months. Excludes simple maintenance depots or minor sub-component repairs that do not constitute an assembly or manufacturing line.

cases.name: Pakistan Babur series (derived from technology transfer/reverse engineering)
India BrahMos (joint venture production established post-transfer)
Taiwan Hsiung的风/Wan Chien variants (domestic scaling of imported tech base)
Ukraine Neptune development (post-2014 domestic missile industrial base scaling)
Saudi Arabia Project 721 (missile manufacturing infrastructure setup with foreign assistance)
Iran Soumar/Quds series (reverse engineering and domestic production of foreign cruise missile designs)
South Korea Hyunmoo cruise/ballistic variants (indigenization of foreign-assisted tech)
Georgia (received systems, no domestic production attempted)
Syria (received anti-ship/cruise systems, no domestic production line established)

coverage_note: 9 named; believed roughly 12 in total for high-end precision missile transfers to sovereign states with pre-existing industrial bases.
known_gaps: Classified bilateral transfers and secret domestic production programs that lack public confirmation.
validity_reason: Defense industrial base transfer dynamics and technology absorption rates change slowly over decades.
